summary: WebFetch reached most first-party provider pages this run, but about a third of lookups failed (HTTP 403 from oracle.com, upcloud.com, godaddy.com; empty response from openmetal.io) and were left out rather than guessed at. Of the 45-item weekly verification batch, 37 slugs were re-confirmed as active against their own current pages with no change needed (checked_active); 5 batch slugs could not be verified this run (openmetal, upcloud, oracle-container-instances, oracle-oke, godaddy-hosting) and are omitted rather than assumed unchanged; 'replit' (the bare provider record, as opposed to replit-deployments) was also left unchecked since its own URL was not independently fetched. Two status alerts are raised from first-party evidence read this run: platform.sh now redirects to Upsun's site, whose own dated CEO blog post describes Platform.sh 'evolving' into Upsun -- this likely means the catalog's existing separate 'upsun' record needs manual reconciliation, not that Upsun is merely a sibling product. hathora.dev now redirects to an unrelated company's site (gamefabric.com) that never mentions Hathora; a third-party blog's separate claim that Fireworks AI acquired Hathora was NOT corroborated by any first-party page and is explicitly flagged as unverified. Two new low-confidence candidates (Blaxel, Inferless) are proposed as products of the existing 'baseten' record, based on each one's own site stating it has 'joined Baseten.' Several other discovery leads (Hosting.com's new AI hosting platform, AventureCloudz, AGBCLOUD, Lyceum, the still-pre-launch Rocketeers) surfaced only in search snippets or third-party press releases this run -- their own official pages were not fetched, so none are proposed; they are candidates for a future run instead of being asserted on secondhand evidence.

status_alerts.rationale: platform.sh now 301-redirects to upsun.com. Upsun's own dated CEO blog post ('Platform.sh is now Upsun', 23 Sep 2025) states Platform.sh 'is evolving and will become Upsun,' with existing customers, pricing, contracts, and support carrying over unchanged under the new name. The catalog currently carries 'upsun' as a separate active record described as merely 'a newer Platform.sh offering' -- this first-party evidence suggests Upsun is instead Platform.sh's renamed successor, so the two records likely need manual reconciliation (not an automatic merge, per policy).

hathora.dev (the catalog's canonical URL) now permanently 301-redirects to gamefabric.com, operated by an unrelated company (marbis GmbH) whose current homepage makes no mention of Hathora at all. This is first-party evidence of a material change (the original product no longer resolves at its canonical URL), but the exact nature -- acquisition, shutdown, or migration -- could not be confirmed from either page, so this is flagged for manual review rather than asserting a specific outcome. Note a third-party blog separately claimed Hathora was acquired by Fireworks AI; that claim is NOT corroborated by any first-party page read this run and should not be relied on.
